title: How do you name the angles marked in a figure?
description: A figure has the point T with rays going to P, Q and R, and curves are marked at T. Each curve is read by the two rays it joins, and each angle is named with T in the middle.
teaching_notes: One idea: read each marked curve by the two arms it joins, then name the angle with the vertex as the middle letter. Watch for students who put the vertex letter first or last.

source: Name the angles marked in the given figure.
video_script.why: The child reads each marked curve by the two arms it joins, and names the angle with the vertex T in the middle.
video_script.substitution: Read each curve at T by the two rays it joins, and write the name with T in the middle.
video_script.anchor: a figure with the point T and the rays TP, TQ and TR, with two curves marked at T
video_script.payoff_line: The marked angles are R T Q and R T P

final_answer.value: The marked angles are angle RTQ and angle RTP
final_answer.spoken: the marked angles are R T Q and R T P

never_show: the names of the marked angles, before the answer beat
maths_rules: All the rays start at T, so T is the vertex of every angle in the figure.
Each marked curve joins two rays, and these two rays are the arms of that angle.
The vertex is the middle letter in the name of an angle.
One curve joins the rays TR and TQ, so that angle is RTQ.
The other curve joins the rays TR and TP, so that angle is RTP.
video_script.design: One idea: read each curve by the two rays it joins, and write the vertex in the middle. The figure stays on the board and each curve lights up in turn. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the arms and the vertex of an angle.
open_questions: The figure is not visible in the extracted text. The worklist describes the point T with rays to P, Q and R and curved marks at T, and gives the printed answer RTQ and RTP, so the video follows that. Please confirm which curves are marked.
